---
title: "Plan: set up the remote GitHub repo and audit public readiness"
author: "Yun Jiang"
date: 2026-10-26
---

# Objective

The remote `jiangyun-fun/pairloom` already existed (private, in sync with
local `main`). Apply the production defaults — license, CI, Dependabot,
repo settings, branch protection, topics — and audit whether the repo is
ready to become public. The repo stays private; flipping visibility is
the owner's decision after the audit.

# Recon findings (before change)

1. Remote existed, private, default branch `main`, no license, no CI;
   local `main` fully pushed.
2. No secrets and no credential-named files in the full git history; no
   internal IPs or hostnames in tracked files.
3. Internal pixi channels (`file:///bioproj/...`, `s3://conda/sibio`)
   appear only as channel listing in `pixi.lock`; every package URL is
   public `conda.anaconda.org`.
4. `pyproject.toml` Homepage pointed at the nonexistent
   `jiangyunacw/pairloom`; the real owner is `jiangyun-fun`.
5. `rust/Cargo.toml` had no `license` field; no LICENSE file existed.
6. Internal references (`/bioproj` paths) sit in 2 docs files plus
   `pixi.toml`/`pixi.lock`; instrument/run IDs appear in 2 docs files.
   History retains them.
7. An untracked `examples/` directory appeared mid-task (concurrent
   user work); it was left out of every commit.

# Steps (as executed)

1. Added `LICENSE` (MIT, 2026, Yun Jiang); set `rust/Cargo.toml`
   `license = "MIT"`; fixed the `pyproject.toml` Homepage URL and added
   Repository/Issues. Commit `5853abd`.
2. README: CI + license badges, real clone URL plus the required
   `pixi run core` step, stale test count fixed (182 → 242), LICENSE
   link. Commit `dbaa9e2`.
3. Added `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — one job named `ci` on `main`
   pushes and PRs: checkout@v7, setup-pixi@v0 (cache), rust-toolchain,
   rust-cache (`workspaces: rust`), then `pixi run core / lint / format
   / test`. Majors resolved from the registry this session. Commit
   `6f242da`.
4. Added `.github/dependabot.yml` — `pip` (root), `cargo` (`/rust`),
   `github-actions`; weekly, grouped. Commit `9232d5a`.
5. Pushed `f4e8402..9232d5a` to `origin/main`.
6. GitHub settings: the first PATCH carried a typo'd field
   (`allow_rebege_merge`) that the REST API silently ignored, leaving
   rebase merges on; a corrective PATCH completed the set
   (squash-only, delete-branch-on-merge, wiki/projects off).
   Description, homepage, and 9 topics set via `gh repo edit`.
7. Branch protection: **blocked** — the API returned 403 "Upgrade to
   GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature."
   The exact PUT payload is recorded in the report; it must run right
   after the repo goes public.
8. Watched the CI run: **green on the first run** (run 40339586894 on
   `9232d5a`) — pixi installed from the committed lock without touching
   the internal channels, the Rust core built, lint/format passed, all
   242 tests passed on the clean runner.
9. Release workflow: deferred. `pixi run build` packages Python only —
   the wheel omits the required Rust core, so release artifacts would
   be broken. Recorded as a next item.

# Files touched

- `LICENSE` (new), `pyproject.toml`, `rust/Cargo.toml`, `README.md`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new), `.github/dependabot.yml` (new)
- `docs/plans/20261026-222311_setup-github-repo.{plan,report}.qmd`
- `docs/misc/requirements_audit.qmd`,
  `docs/misc/next_and_recommendation.qmd`

# Risks and outcomes

1. Internal channels breaking CI install-from-lock: did not happen
   (all package URLs public; run green).
2. Rust toolchain missing on CI: handled by the rust-toolchain action
   before `pixi run core`.
3. Branch protection on a private free-plan repo: blocked by plan
   (403); deferred to the public flip, payload recorded.

# Verification

1. CI run 40339586894: conclusion `success`, all steps `success`.
2. Repo settings verified via API echo: squash only, rebase/merge off,
   delete-on-merge on, wiki/projects off; license detected as MIT;
   description/homepage/topics present.
3. Protection: verified unavailable (403 on GET too) — matches the
   free-private-plan limitation.
4. Public-readiness verdict: no blockers; flagged items are internal
   paths/sample IDs in tracked files (history retains them) and the
   internal pixi channels for fresh solves.
